13	## Problem Statement
14	
15	DDX Agent has the right ownership boundary for shared model policy, but the
16	current catalog is still incomplete as an operational system:
17	
18	- the embedded manifest is stale and too small to serve as a real shared policy
19	  source
20	- the only implemented refresh path is a manual local override file
21	- there is no versioned published manifest channel outside normal binary
22	  releases
23	- the current manifest shape is too narrow for the intended cross-surface
24	  policy tiers because one logical tier may map to different concrete model
25	  families and different effort defaults on different surfaces
26	
27	The immediate product need is to support a current coding-policy baseline with
28	three stable levels:
29	
30	- `code-high`: `opus-4.7` / `gpt-5.4` at `high` effort
31	- `code-medium`: `sonnet-4.6` / `gpt-5.4-mini` at `medium` effort
32	- `code-economy`: `haiku-5.5` at `medium` effort and `qwen3.5-27b` at `high`
33	  effort
34	
35	The broader system goal is to make the catalog publishable and updateable on a
36	faster cadence than `ddx-agent` binary releases while preserving the existing
37	runtime constraint that ordinary request execution does not fetch policy from
38	the network.
39	
40	## Requirements
41	
42	### Functional
43	
44	- Keep `modelcatalog/catalog/models.yaml` as the canonical source manifest in
45	  this repo.
46	- Publish a versioned, immutable manifest bundle independently of binary
47	  releases whenever catalog policy changes.
48	- Publish a stable channel pointer so `ddx-agent`, DDx, and operators can fetch
49	  the latest approved manifest without guessing artifact names.
50	- Preserve the embedded manifest snapshot in `ddx-agent` releases for offline
51	  deterministic behavior.
52	- Add an explicit local update workflow so operators can install or refresh a
53	  local manifest file without editing YAML by hand.
54	- Keep the runtime request path offline-by-default. A normal `Run()` or
55	  `ddx-agent run ...` invocation must never fetch the manifest from the
56	  network.
57	- Allow DDx and `ddx-agent` to consume the same published manifest file.
58	- Evolve the manifest schema so one logical policy tier can project to
59	  different concrete models and effort defaults per surface.
60	- Refresh the starter catalog so it exposes current code-oriented tiers:
61	  `code-high`, `code-medium`, and `code-economy`.
62	- Preserve compatibility aliases during migration:
63	  - `smart -> code-high`
64	  - `fast -> code-medium`
65	  - `cheap -> code-economy`

67	### Non-Functional
68	
69	- Published manifests must be deterministic, content-addressable, and checksum
70	  verifiable.
71	- A stale or missing external manifest must not break ordinary runtime use; the
72	  embedded snapshot remains the safe fallback.
73	- The distribution path should be simple enough for DDx to mirror locally or in
74	  CI without needing to parse GitHub HTML or binary release assets.
75	- Schema evolution must be explicit and versioned so older binaries can reject
76	  unsupported manifest shapes cleanly.
77	
78	### Constraints
79	
80	- `agent.Run()` still receives one resolved concrete provider per attempt.
81	- HELIX continues to emit intent only; it does not fetch or own manifest
82	  distribution.
83	- DDx remains the cross-harness router. Embedded `ddx-agent` owns only embedded
84	  provider selection and embedded-surface catalog projection.

88	### Decision 1: Separate source manifest from published catalog bundle
89	
90	- **Question**: How should catalog policy be distributed faster than binary
91	  releases?
92	- **Alternatives**:
93	  - rely only on the embedded manifest
94	  - require users to copy the repo YAML manually
95	  - publish a versioned catalog bundle from manifest-only changes
96	- **Chosen**: keep the repo YAML as source of truth and publish a versioned
97	  catalog bundle plus a stable channel pointer from a dedicated catalog
98	  workflow
99	- **Rationale**: the source manifest remains reviewable in git, while consumers

10	LLM loop with file read/write, shell execution, navigation helpers, and
11	structured I/O. Designed to be embedded in
12	[DDx](https://github.com/DocumentDrivenDX/ddx) and other build orchestrators.
